course.title: Next.js — Complete Practical Full-Stack Web Development Course
course.description: A deep practical Next.js course covering App Router, layouts, dynamic routes, Server and Client Components, data fetching, caching, route handlers, mutations, authentication, styling, security, performance, testing, deployment and a complete student learning platform.
learningOutcomes: Master App Router and file-based routing.
Build nested layouts and dynamic routes.
Build route handlers and server mutations.
Create accessible forms and UX states.
Build responsive course and lesson experiences.
Implement progress and task submission flows.
Apply performance, testing, security and deployment practices.
Build a production-style student learning platform.

notes.text: What Is Next.js?
Understand Next.js as a React framework and learn why routing, rendering, data fetching and deployment are integrated into the framework.

notes.caption: Visual explanation of What Is Next.js?.

Build production web applications with React.

notes.text: Study Method

items: Inspect the browser and server output.
Test loading, empty and error states.

notes.title: Next.js Tip
notes.text: Understand where code runs. Server Components, Client Components, route handlers and server-side data access have different responsibilities.

notes.title: Common Mistake
notes.text: Do not add 'use client' to every component. Keep server-rendered logic on the server when possible and send only interactive parts to the client.

lessons.title: Server Actions
lessons.description: Use server actions for server-side mutations when they fit the application architecture.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a realistic production application.

notes.text: Server Actions
Use server actions for server-side mutations when they fit the application architecture.

notes.caption: Visual explanation of Server Actions.

notes.code:
async function enroll(){'use server';console.log('Enroll student')}
export default function Enroll(){return <form action={enroll}><button>Enroll Now</button></form>}

notes.text: Study Method

items: Inspect the browser and server output.
Test loading, empty and error states.

notes.title: Next.js Tip
notes.text: Understand where code runs. Server Components, Client Components, route handlers and server-side data access have different responsibilities.

notes.title: Common Mistake
notes.text: Do not add 'use client' to every component. Keep server-rendered logic on the server when possible and send only interactive parts to the client.

practicals.objective: Apply Server Actions in a small Next.js feature.

practicals.expectedOutput: A working Next.js feature demonstrating the lesson.
